DEVIATION FROM THE BRIEF, deliberate: the brief and the card both say 'clear AND unref at both sites'. I did not add unref; I REMOVED the one at the shutdown site. #4813 already landed the opposite finding in this same file -- an unref'd guard stops pinning the loop but stops being a guard too, so a hung teardown in an otherwise-idle process exits silently at status 0 and never reaches 'Shutdown timed out -- forcing exit'/exit(1). Reclaiming on settle gets the loop hygiene unref was reaching for without giving up the guarantee, so the two goals were never in tension. Ablation C below is the pin that catches the brief's version. THREE MORE BRIEF/CARD CLAIMS THAT DID NOT HOLD, none blocking: (1) 'Re-derive the line numbers; kernel.ts may have moved since b34ef8de8' -- it had NOT moved. raceStartupTimeout is still 629-647 and shutdown still 457-469, and all four frames reproduced at exactly 636:32 / 643:34 / 461:36 / 469:27. I wrote a duplicate of the shutdown one before finding #5274's and deleted it in the second commit rather than ship two near-identical tests. (3) the DoD's per-package `pnpm typecheck` does not exist for @objectstack/core (scripts are build/test only); `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core typecheck` fails loudly with ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_NO_SCRIPT, not the silent zero-match exit-0 trap.
